options.text: A seed can be classed with living things: under suitable conditions it germinates and grows.
A dry seed that later sprouts under suitable conditions was living while dry.
A wooden pencil is living because it came from a plant that grew from a seed.
A dry seed that has not yet sprouted must be non-living.

stem:
Anika keeps dry moong seeds in a jar. Later she soaks some on moist cotton and they sprout.

Which claims correctly classify a seed after considering germination? One or more options may be correct.

teacher.key_rationale: A seed that can germinate under suitable conditions is living, including while dry. A wooden pencil is not living. Lack of sprouting yet does not prove a seed is non-living.
